transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-15
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Marcus Feldman, Priya Desai (Redwood); Ravi Patel, Sofia Nguyen, Daniel Kim, Maya Lopez (Orion)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Quick status: networking stable but observed two small latency spikes correlated to egress shaping; kernel upgrade v3b staged in canary, need rollback procedure tightened.

Topics:

Action items (quick list): Marcus to send patch; Sofia to upload pcap; Lena to schedule canary run; Daniel to confirm KMS rotation policy.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Okay, um, let's kick off. Thanks everybody for joining, we've got about 50 minutes so we'll go through wins first then the open items. Marcus, can you run us through the night soak?
[00:18] Marcus Feldman: Yeah, sure. So last night we ran the 6 hour soak at nominal load plus the 20% spike. Overall throughput held, tokens/sec stable, but we saw three tail latency blips around 02:14 UTC that correlated with a spiky egress queue on Orion's side — looks like your egress shaping triggered the circuit breaker for, uh, roughly 4 to 6 seconds.
[00:38] Ravi Patel: Right, that was the egress policy we have on the border router. We set a strict shaping for the POC VLAN to protect other services, so that, that was expected, maybe. The weird bit was the second spike coincided with a KV cache miss storm, like more than one worker trying to warm the cache at once.
[00:59] Marcus Feldman: Exactly, and the cache warmup paired with egress backpressure made the request pacing a little jittery. We noticed also one of the hosts hit a higher syscall latency after the kernel bump we rolled Friday night — it's subtle but it amplifies under the mixed workload.
[01:21] Sofia Nguyen: Wait, the kernel bump — was that the v3b quant patch? We thought that was just an inference runtime change.
[01:30] Marcus Feldman: Ah, sorry. There were two changes: a runtime quantization tweak and the low-latency kernel patch v3b — the latter adjusts the netdev tx path for smaller bursts. We rolled it to the canary group.
[01:42] Maya Lopez: I can confirm on ops that the canary host with v3b saw slightly higher syscall wait during synthetic loads. Not a full regression but consistent.
[01:52] Lena Ortiz: Ok let's slow down — we don't want to conflate the two. Marcus, can you summarize the risk if we push v3b wider without a rollback plan?
[02:03] Marcus Feldman: Risk is mostly tail-latency penalties under bursty egress. Without a fast rollback you'd see a hit to p50-p99 and potential transient 5-10% error rate if circuit breakers trip. We need an automated, low-touch rollback (drain then revert) and a playbook for on-call.
[02:23] Daniel Kim: From security perspective, we also need to ensure the new kernel doesn't change our audit hooks or cause any unexpected debuginfo leak. Can you provide audit-log samples before/after?
[02:36] Marcus Feldman: Yeah, we'll capture sample logs. Note though the transcription of syscalls into audit logs is sometimes noisy, so we'll redact sensitive fields.
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: Great. Let's move to the soak numbers — can someone share the high-level table?
[02:52] Marcus Feldman: I posted a short result sheet in the shared drive: average latency 78ms, p95 220ms, p99 480ms, but the 3 blips pushed p99 to 720ms briefly. Token cost per request didn't change meaningfully. I'll upload the diffs comparing pre-v3 and post-v3 canary.
[03:14] Ravi Patel: And on our side infrastructure CPU saw a small bump on the canary host, likely because the kernel path touched irq handling.
[03:24] Priya Desai: Noted. Do we have the exact times so Orion can pull PCAPs?
[03:29] Marcus Feldman: Times are in the sheet, but the main ones are 02:14:16, 02:27:40 and 03:02:05 UTC.
[03:36] Sofia Nguyen: We'll extract pcap for those timestamps and upload. Also I'll include netstat and ifconfig snapshots.
[03:43] Maya Lopez: We'll try to reproduce in our staging by toggling the egress shaping. If we can trigger the same KV cache storm that'll help isolate.
[03:50] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. On KV cache: Marcus, are there any short term config knobs we can change to avoid the warmup thundering herd?
[03:58] Marcus Feldman: Yeah, we can stagger the warmup with jitter and reduce simultaneous fetches, and raise the soft TTL during cold starts. Also enable progressive prefill for hot prefixes. We'll send a suggested config diff.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: We can do the stagger and TTL changes easily. Would prefer if you give the exact YAML snippet so our ops don't guess.
[04:19] Marcus Feldman: Will do.
[04:21] [04:21] Lena Ortiz: Switching to routing — BGP sessions looked fine?
[04:26] Maya Lopez: BGP flaps not observed but we did see micro-congestion on the egress link at 10Gbps when the soak hit burst windows.
[04:33] Marcus Feldman: That aligns with our observation — the link is saturating briefly and the shaping pushes packets into a queue which triggers the CB. Two mitigation ideas: increase egress headroom for the POC VLAN or implement per-flow pacing on our side to smooth peaks.
[04:50] Sofia Nguyen: We can't increase headroom globally. Maybe allow short burst windows for Redwood traffic only? We can do QoS policy by DSCP.
[04:58] Daniel Kim: If QoS by DSCP is used, we need to ensure it's documented for compliance and that audit logs capture the mapping.
[05:07] Lena Ortiz: Marcus, can Redwood implement client-side pacing as an interim fix?
[05:11] Marcus Feldman: Yes, we have a lightweight pacing layer we can enable per-route. It reduces peak token generation rate and smooths bursts. There is a small latency tradeoff — p50 up about 10ms — but p99 improves.
[05:25] Ravi Patel: Ok we'll try DSCP mapping for the POC VLAN and run a controlled burst to see the effect.
[05:32] Lena Ortiz: Great. Next, rollback plan for kernel v3b. Marcus?
[05:37] Marcus Feldman: We have an automated rollout that supports canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% but for rollback we recommend: 1) drain canary, 2) revert kernel package on canary host image, 3) validate with smoke tests, 4) roll forward with reduced concurrency. I'll prepare step-by-step and a one-click script we can run via your orchestration.
[05:57] Maya Lopez: Can you make the script compatible with our jumpbox workflow? We can't allow arbitrary SSH from Redwood.
[06:05] Marcus Feldman: We'll make it push-based and require an SSM session or your approved runner. No direct SSH.
[06:11] Daniel Kim: Need to ensure any scripts are signed and we have SHA sums for the packages.
[06:17] Marcus Feldman: Absolutely. We'll publish signed artifacts and checksums.
[06:21] Priya Desai: Quick Q: how does this interact with our KV cache prefill? If we roll back, do we need to flush caches?
[06:28] Marcus Feldman: Flushing is usually unnecessary; we recommend draining and letting workers warm gradually. However if you prefer a deterministic state, we can provide a cache reset command.
[06:38] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Let's touch on telemetry: Daniel, did you get the audit-log sample we sent last week?
[06:45] Daniel Kim: Yes, we reviewed. We want one more sample with the v3b canary traffic so we can vet any extra fields. Also request: include correlation IDs at token level in the sample so our compliance team can map requests to user flows.
[07:00] Marcus Feldman: We can include a correlation header. Note that PII will be redacted.
[07:05] Daniel Kim: Good. Also confirm retention: 90 days for infra logs and 365 days for audit-level events?
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: That's our standard enterprise offering for pilots but we can adjust; we'll send the exact retention table.
[07:18] Sofia Nguyen: One small note: during the night soak a bunch of HTTP 429s were returned for a downstream service chain. Those were internal retries from our side but surfaced as upstream errors.
[07:29] Marcus Feldman: That could explain the spikes, increased retry storm. We should instrument retry budgets and maybe reduce client retry count.
[07:37] Ravi Patel: We'll check our retry logic.
[07:40] Lena Ortiz: Good. Next item: can we schedule the bigger canary run? I propose Jan 20 with 1.5x concurrency.
[07:48] Sofia Nguyen: Jan 20 works for us but prefer morning window 09:00 UTC.
[07:53] Lena Ortiz: I'll book 09:00 UTC Jan 20. Marcus will prepare patch and rollback doc before then.
[07:59] Marcus Feldman: I'll aim to send the patch and the one-click rollback by Monday 18th end of day.
[08:06] Lena Ortiz: Action item recap — Marcus patch+rollback; Sofia pcap; Daniel audit; Lena schedule. Anything else?
[08:14] Maya Lopez: One more: can we get a small failover test on interconnect so we can validate the BGP re-route behavior?
[08:22] Ravi Patel: Sure, we can schedule a micro-failover in staging during the canary window.
[08:27] Lena Ortiz: Excellent. Open Q&A:
[08:30] Daniel Kim: Two quick security questions: 1) are there any new ports opened by v3b? 2) does the patch require additional kernel modules?
[08:38] Marcus Feldman: No new external ports. It touches the tx path and one optional module but it's built-in in our images. We'll list modules.
[08:44] Daniel Kim: Ok please include that in the doc.
[08:47] Sofia Nguyen: On the perf tuning front, could Redwood lower initial batch size for cold starts to reduce p99?
[08:53] Marcus Feldman: Yes, small initial batch sizes help; we can make batching adaptive. It slightly increases CPU load but improves tail latency.
[09:01] Ravi Patel: That might also help when you add pacing — combined should smooth the worst-case.
[09:07] Lena Ortiz: Let's close with a crisp next steps and owners.
[09:11] Marcus Feldman: I'll send patch + rollback steps (owner: Marcus; due: 2026-01-18).
[09:15] Sofia Nguyen: We'll upload pcap and net snapshots for listed timestamps (owner: Sofia; due: 2026-01-20).
[09:19] Daniel Kim: We'll review audit sample and KMS rotation impact (owner: Daniel; due: 2026-01-22).
[09:24] Lena Ortiz: I'll schedule the Jan 20 canary at 09:00 UTC and invite ops (owner: Lena; due: 2026-01-16).
[09:30] Priya Desai: I'll follow up on docs and make sure everything is in the shared drive.
[09:36] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Anything else before we drop?
[09:39] Maya Lopez: No, thanks everyone.
[09:41] Ravi Patel: Thanks.
[09:43] Lena Ortiz: End.
